On the maintenance of small tools

A tool that does one thing tends to outlive the framework it was written against. This is not a moral claim about simplicity; it is an observation about surface area.

The cost of a dependency

Every dependency is a bet that someone else will keep caring. Most of those bets are fine. A few are not, and the ones that are not tend to fail at the least convenient moment.

Measured over four years, the median unmaintained transitive dependency in our tree was introduced by a package we chose for a single function.
